riscos.descricao: Execuções repetidas do mesmo prompt podem gerar saídas diferentes, o que poderia afetar as variáveis dependentes e a estabilidade dos achados.
Viés do juiz: a avaliação de utilidade e correção pelo ICE-Score com GPT-4.1-mini pode introduzir vieses específicos do modelo; o estudo também discute autoviés e viés de família em LLM-as-a-judge.

riscos.descricao: Desenho observacional: o estudo identifica associações estatísticas, não causalidade, e reconhece possíveis fatores de confusão; o poder explicativo dos modelos é moderado (pseudo R2 entre 0.107 e 0.159).
Viés de dados: um único contribuidor respondia por mais de 80% das conversas, o que violaria a independência das observações e enviesaria as estatísticas.

Validade de constructo: dados minerados de repositórios abertos podem ter qualidade questionável; erros de pré-processamento e filtragem; ausência de pré-processamento do código pode influenciar a similaridade de cosseno.
Validade externa e temporal: apenas prompts em inglês, conversas públicas do ChatGPT no GitHub, tarefas de manutenção e evolução, conversas de turno único e coleta no início de 2025.

citacoes.trecho: We conducted an empirical study of real-world, single-turn interactions between developers and ChatGPT collected from GITHUB.

Regression analysis shows that readability metrics are strong predictors of usefulness and correctness, whereas structural features such as the number of sentences and task type significantly affect conceptual consistency.
We operationalized this dimension with a boolean value that indicates whether the prompt contains code examples or snippets.

citacoes.trecho: The metric was thus defined over the three remaining patterns, Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Chain-of-Thought, and coded as a binary variable, where 1 indicates that the prompt follows one of these patterns and 0 otherwise.

citacoes.trecho: In this stage, we decided to remove the Prompt Pattern metric, since the manual classification revealed that 90% of the prompts (164 out of 183) were Zero-shot.
After this adjustment, the dataset stabilized at a final set of 183 conversations (39 from commits, 138 from pull requests, and 6 from issues), extracted from 94 distinct GitHub repositories.

A possible explanation is that corrective tasks, such as bug fixing, are inherently more complex than perfective tasks, such as extending or generating code, which makes them harder for LLMs to handle.

Regarding task type, additive and corrective tasks showed positive coefficients compared to the perfective baseline, with corrective tasks approaching significance (p = 0.084), while preventive tasks were positively associated but non-significant.

citacoes.trecho: Both readability metrics—Flesch Reading Ease and Gunning Fog Index—were significantly and positively associated with correctness, indicating that prompts that are clearer and structurally more complex tended to yield more correct code.
Initial tests revealed violations of the proportional odds assumption for the number of difficult words and sentences.
Through the elicitation procedure, we selected seven independent variables covering both readability-related and structural properties of prompts.
Together, these eight variables capture complementary dimensions of prompt formulation.
After completing this step, we measured the three readability variables on the natural language text of each prompt.
With seven predictors and five ordered response categories (0–4), this implies a conservative requirement of N ≥ 70 conversations.
In cases where the two reviewers disagreed, an external reviewer was involved to provide clarification and resolve the conflict.
For example, each dataset entry was labeled by at least two authors independently, and disagreements were resolved by a third author.
Although the original formulation of ICE-Score employed GPT-4, in our study we opted for GPT-4.1-mini.

In line with the guidelines for SE studies using LLMs by Baltes et al. [97], we report that the LLM temperature was set to 0, and for prompting we used the original prompt setup reported by Zhuo et al. [34].
Another potential threat comes from the non-determinism of LLMs, as repeated executions of the same prompt may yield different outputs.
To mitigate this, we relied on a fixed dataset of already-executed conversations, ensuring that the analysis was performed on stable outcomes rather than re-generated outputs.
Our study identifies statistical associations between prompt characteristics and output quality, but it does not establish causality.

To mitigate the risk of overstating our findings, we carefully framed results in correlational terms, verified robustness across multiple model specifications, and excluded variables that violated model assumptions.
Moreover, the moderate explanatory power of our models (0.107 < pseudo-R2 <0.159) indicates that prompt-oriented metrics account for only part of the variability in output quality.
Finally, an initial exploratory analysis revealed that a single contributor accounted for more than 80% of the conversations.
Specifically, we computed the mean number of conversations per contributor and constrained over-represented contributors to this threshold (10 conversations).

Another potential limitation came from the evaluation of usefulness and correctness through ICE-Score with GPT-4.1-mini as the judging model, which may have introduced model-specific biases; we mitigated this by selecting a strong and widely adopted evaluator and by ensuring methodological transparency to enable replication with alternative judges.
We addressed this by inspecting the scripts used for data collection and processing and by manually validating a sample of the dataset.

Finally, we did not preprocess code (e.g., comment removal, normalization) before computing conceptual consistency between LLM-generated and developer-adapted code snippets, which may influence similarity scores.

In all such cases, an iterative strategy that progressively refines and validates outputs may be preferable to relying on a single response, whereas perfective tasks may already yield satisfactory results with simpler interactions.
The two prompts differ only in surface form, yet only the readable one yielded code that a developer could adopt without further intervention.
